title: Adaptive stride-based slot allocation + KV-shard prefetch orchestration for mixed-length continuous batching
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem statement: production workloads with mixed short prompts and long responses suffer from two correlated issues: (1) the continuous batcher slots are fragmented by stride mismatches when short and long sequences interleave, increasing tail latency and reducing packing efficiency; (2) KV cache shards get unevenly populated causing excessive eviction churn and GPU memory fragmentation during long-response generations. Both reduce effective throughput and increase cost-per-token.

Goal: implement an adaptive 'stride + prefetch' scheduler that coordinates slot allocation stride with per-slot KV-shard prefetching and a lightweight GPU compaction hint to reduce fragmentation. The scheduler should: (a) detect workload length bimodality dynamically, (b) adapt slot stride windows to cluster similar-length requests without increasing average latency for short queries, (c) prefetch KV-shard ranges for long-response seeds to reduce on-demand page faults, and (d) periodically trigger cooperative compaction hints to the GPU allocator for heavily fragmented pages. Target metrics: reduce p99 tail latency for mixed workloads by >= 20% (baseline p99 420ms -> <= 336ms) for 512-token responses, improve batching token throughput by >= 10%, and reduce measured GPU memory fragmentation metric from ~18% to <8%.

Design highlights and trade-offs: 
- Stride-based slot allocation: use a sliding window of slot stride S that adapts between 1 and 8 based on short/long ratio over a 30s moving window. Smaller S prioritizes short-query latency; larger S packs similar-length long requests to maximize KV locality. Trade-off: larger S may increase latency for isolated short queries; mitigated with an emergency fast-path that steals a slot when observed latency crosses configurable thresholds.
- KV-shard prefetching: maintain per-session predicted KV ranges derived from prefix length and model architecture heuristics. On scheduling a candidate long-generation slot, issue an async prefetch for top-K shard ranges (K=3 default) using a bounded prefetch queue per-GPU to avoid saturating PCIe. Trade-off: prefetch increases memory pressure; controlled by adaptive K and eviction thresholds.
- GPU compaction hinting: do not attempt intrusive GC. Instead, emit compaction hints at low priority during idle gaps (observed GPU utilization < 20% for 200ms). The allocator accepts the hint and tries to coalesce small free blocks. This reduces fragmentation without impacting throughput.

Instrumentation: add Grafana panels for: slot stride distribution, KV prefetch queue length, KV prefetch hit latency, per-shard eviction rate, GPU fragmentation %, p50/p95/p99 latency split by short/long class, tokens/sec. See artifacts for example panels.

Success criteria: measurable improvements on canary traffic (see rollout) and no regression on short-request p50 latency or CPU utilization.

updates: 2026-02-25 Aisha Malik - Created ticket and initial spec draft. Added baseline measurement links and requirement targets.

2026-03-02 Gunnar Lee - Spike completed: implemented prototype 'stride-v0' and measured basic packing improvements (+6% tokens/sec) but saw increased short-p99 by ~35ms in high short-query tails. Added emergency fast-path idea.
2026-03-05 Priya Suresh - Design review notes: prefer bounded async prefetch queue and per-GPU prefetch budgeting to avoid PCIe saturation; recommend per-model K tuning knob exposed in config.

2026-03-07 Gunnar Lee - Implemented KV-shard predictor and prefetch queue; internal perf run on staging: +11% tokens/sec, p99 down 14% for mixed workload, GPU fragmentation unchanged. Noted increased device memory footprint ~2.3%.
2026-03-10 Security Team - Quick read: no new data exfiltration vectors introduced by prefetching; confirmed prefetch requests respect tenancy/namespace headers.
2026-03-12 Aisha Malik - Added compaction hint flow; ran compaction in low-util windows on test cluster: fragmentation dropped from 19% -> 9% after 2h continuous runs; validated no throughput impact.
2026-03-14 Gunnar Lee - Preparing canary rollout config and PRs. PRs: runtime#2791 (scheduler), runtime#2820 (kv prefetch), runtime#2837 (compaction hint). Added gating metrics and alert thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deployment (1% traffic) shows >=12% token/sec improvement for mixed workload without >5% regression in short-query p50 latency.
KV prefetch hit latency median < 8ms on canary and prefetch queue saturation < 5% during peak.
GPU fragmentation metric reduced to <10% on canary hosts within 4 hours of canary start without increased OOM events.
Instrumentation panels and alerts created and validated: stride distribution, prefetch queue, per-shard eviction, fragmentation, latency split.
Code reviews completed and security checklist signed off.
Rollout runbook documented with rollback steps and synthetic load tests.
test_plan: Unit tests for stride scheduler logic and emergency fast-path.
Integration tests for async prefetch queue correctness and backpressure behavior (simulate PCIe delay).
Chaos test: introduce artificial long-request spikes and verify adaptive stride increases S and then decays back appropriately.
Performance A/B: run mixed workload harness (30% short 30-64 tokens, 70% long 256-512 tokens) across baseline vs feature for 24 hours; collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
Memory soak: 6-hour run on staging cluster with compaction hints enabled and disabled; monitor fragmentation, OOMs, and eviction rates.
rollout_plan: Canary 1% traffic for 6 hours with synthetic canary load + real traffic sampling. Monitor gating metrics every 15 minutes.
If canary OK, ramp to 10% for 8 hours. Continue monitoring.
Stage rollout to Dedicated pools first (predictable capacity) before Hosted API; ramp to 100% in 4 steps with 30m observation windows.
Rollback: toggle scheduler flag off and drain prefetch queue; explicit GPU compaction hint disabled to avoid interfering with baseline allocator.
Post-rollout: run 48h verification and capture final perf reports.
